precepts.text: The Most High warned Israel would be carried to a nation they knew not, and there serve other gods, wood and stone.
precepts.point: The heathen open their mouths to set forth the praises of idols and to magnify a fleshly king for ever. The Persians, Assyrians, and Egyptians all magnified themselves when they were in power.
precepts.why:
Esther confesses the true reason for the captivity: “we have sinned before thee: therefore hast thou given us into the hands of our enemies, Because we worshipped their gods: O Lord, thou art righteous.” She does not blame the Persians; she says the Most High is righteous in what he did.

That is exactly what he warned. “The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.” Israel would be carried to a nation they knew not, and there they would serve other gods. Esther in Persia is that warning come to pass, and her confession is the curse owned.

This is the same confession our people must make about why we went into captivity and are under these curses: we sinned, we worshipped their gods, and the Lord is righteous.

precepts.text: The Lord would scatter Israel among all people, and there they would serve other gods, which neither they nor their fathers had known.
precepts.point: The heathen open their mouths to set forth the praises of idols and to magnify a fleshly king for ever. The Persians, Assyrians, and Egyptians all magnified themselves when they were in power.
precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Esther's words, “we worshipped their gods”, are the fulfilling of this. The scattering and the serving of other gods came together, as the Most High said they would, and so she says, “thou art righteous.”

Yet the enemy is not satisfied with that. “Nevertheless it satisfieth them not, that we are in bitter captivity: but they have stricken hands with their idols, That they will abolish the thing that thou with thy mouth hast ordained, and destroy thine inheritance, and stop the mouth of them that praise thee”. It is the same thing today: they are not satisfied with us serving in captivity, they want to destroy our people.

And they “open the mouths of the heathen to set forth the praises of the idols, and to magnify a fleshly king for ever.” The Persians, the Assyrians and the Egyptians all magnified themselves when they were in power. The scattered nation serving wood and stone is the nation the heathen magnify themselves over.

moments.label: The Slave Mentality Yesterday & Today: the True Diaspora

points: Hear the voice of the forlorn. That is not a common word, so understand it: lonely, unhappy and miserable, from abandonment or lack of care.
Empty or neglected, describing a place that is run down. That is the ghettos and the slums.
Hopeless, unlikely to succeed or achieve a positive outcome. That is the blindness.

The word comes from the Middle English meaning lost completely, from the Old English verb to lose, abandon or destroy. Forlorn means the lost, and Christ said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, not the lost sheep of everybody.

note.label: The Slave Mentality Yesterday & Today: the True Diaspora

points: Queen Esther, in fear of death, resorted unto the Lord. She laid away her glorious apparel and put on the garments of anguish and mourning, covering her head with ashes instead of precious ointments and humbling her body greatly.
She prayed to the Lord God of Israel, confessing him as her only King and her only helper, for her danger was in her own hand. She was the one who had to go before the king.

From her youth she had heard in the tribe of her family how the Most High took Israel from among all people and their fathers for a perpetual inheritance, and that he performed whatsoever he promised them. She stands on the covenant history she was taught.

Esther confesses the true reason for the captivity: our people sinned before the Most High and were given into the hands of their enemies because they worshipped other gods. She says plainly, O Lord, thou art righteous. This is the same confession our people must make about why we went into captivity and under these curses.

She says the enemy is not satisfied that Israel is in bitter captivity; they have joined hands with their idols to abolish what the Most High ordained, to destroy his inheritance, and to stop the mouth of them that praise him. This is the same thing today: they are not satisfied with us serving in captivity, they want to destroy our people.
The heathen open their mouths to set forth the praises of idols and to magnify a fleshly king for ever. The Persians, Assyrians, and Egyptians all magnified themselves when they were in power.

Esther asks that the Lord give not his sceptre to them that be nothing, and that he turn the device of the enemy upon himself, making an example of the one who began this against us, meaning Haman. The evil he devised she prays would fall upon his own head.

She asks the Most High to make himself known in the time of affliction and to give her boldness before the king, whom she calls the lion. She has to stand before the king to make her request, so she asks for eloquent speech and that the king's heart be turned to hate the one who fights against them.
She pleads to be delivered by the Lord's hand, calling herself desolate with no other helper but the Most High. Her boldness comes from prayer, not from her own position.

Esther tells the Most High that she hates the glory of the unrighteous and abhors the bed of the uncircumcised and of all the heathen. She hated the high estate she carried and wore the crown as a menstruous rag, not wearing it when she was private by herself.

She testifies that she had not eaten at Aman's table nor greatly esteemed the king's feast nor drunk the wine of the drink offerings, and had known no joy since she was brought there except in the Lord God of Abraham. She asks the mighty God above all to hear the forlorn and deliver her out of her fear.
